item.title: Lebanon National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Lebanon National Day

Press Statement

November 22, 2026

The United States of America extends its congratulations to the people of Lebanon on the 83rd anniversary of their independence. The Lebanese people have shown extraordinary talent and resilience, both at home and across their global diaspora. On this occasion, the United States reaffirms its support for a fully sovereign Lebanon, at peace with its neighbors and accountable only to its own citizens. We will continue to stand with the Lebanese people and the Lebanese state, and look forward to growing the partnership between our two nations.

item.title: Sanctioning Iranian Regime Insiders Who Profit from Stolen Oil Wealth
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Sanctioning Iranian Regime Insiders Who Profit from Stolen Oil Wealth

Press Statement

November 20, 2026

Today, the United States took action against four corrupt Iranian regime insiders who illicitly sell oil to help fund the regime’s military and its support for terrorism. Those designated include a former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) intelligence officer and the son of the head of Mahan Air, an airline the regime uses to move weapons and fighters for the IRGC-Qods Force.

Today’s action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, a whole-of-government campaign to cut off illicit money flows that sustain the Iranian regime. The United States will continue working to deny Tehran the revenue it uses to destabilize the region, threaten our partners, and pursue its dangerous ambitions.

Today’s designations are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy, and E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority. For more information, please see Treasury’s Press Release.

item.title: Joint Statement on the Sixth U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting on Science and Technology Cooperation
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the Sixth U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting on Science and Technology Cooperation

Media Note

November 20, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and Germany.

Begin Text

The United States hosted the Federal Republic of Germany in Washington, DC, on November 19-20, 2026, for the 6th U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting (JCM) on Science and Technology Cooperation. The State Department’s Assistant Secretary for European and Eurasian Affairs, Brendan Hanrahan, co-chaired the meeting with Germany’s Dr. Effrosyni Chelioti, Director General for Strategies and Policy Issues and International Affairs and Europe at the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space.

The delegations used this JCM to deepen their cooperation in robotics, fusion energy, biotechnology, and critical minerals recovery. The delegations decided to promote joint research, agency-to-agency partnerships, shared technical standards where appropriate, and public-private collaboration to accelerate the path from scientific discovery to commercial application.

Both delegations reaffirmed the importance of securing the shared research ecosystem, determining to strengthen information-sharing and risk-analysis cooperation via Germany’s National Research Security Platform. The two countries underscored that protecting critical and emerging technologies is essential to safeguarding the integrity of the bilateral research relationship.

Both countries reaffirmed their commitment to a partnership that pairs German research, engineering, and manufacturing excellence with American research and commercialization strength, powering innovation that is mutually beneficial.

End Text

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Secretary Rubio’s Call with UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan

Readout

November 20, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke today with UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan.  The two discussed the need to end the war in Sudan, while Secretary Rubio also emphasized the importance of a humanitarian truce, durable peace, and transition to a civilian government.

item.title: Oman National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Oman National Day

Press Statement

November 20, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend congratulations to His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik and to the people of the Sultanate of Oman on the occasion of your National Day.

As the United States marks 250 years of independence, we commemorate a partnership with Oman that dates back nearly as far, to the presidency of George Washington. Our relationship began with maritime trade and has expanded into energy and emerging technology. With Oman joining the Artemis Accords this year, our cooperation now extends into space exploration.

The United States values its partnership with Oman and will continue to work with the Sultanate towards regional stability. We send our best wishes for a happy National Day and continued prosperity for the Sultanate of Oman.

item.title: First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together Gathers ASEAN First Spouses For Event Hosted by Philippine First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together Gathers ASEAN First Spouses For Event Hosted by Philippine First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos

Media Note

November 19, 2026

On November 16, First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together initiative brought leaders together in Manila for an event focused on child online protection, hosted by Philippine First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos. The event advanced Mrs. Trump’s global leadership to empower children and keep them safe in the digital age.

Mrs. Araneta-Marcos co-hosted the event with the Philippines Child Protection Network. She welcomed visiting ASEAN First Spouses and about 150 leaders from government, civil society, and the private sector, including leading U.S. tech companies, such as Google, Intel, Meta, and Microsoft. A panel of child protection experts and a speaker from Intel shared practical ways to keep children safe online.

U.S. Ambassador Lee Lipton spoke about the strong partnership between the United States and the Philippines to protect children. He pointed to the U.S. Embassy’s close work with Philippine law enforcement, prosecutors, and advocates to fight online crimes against children. He praised Mrs. Trump for turning partnership into action. Ambassador Lipton noted that in just one year she has united nearly 60 First Spouses and equivalent leaders so that no child is held back by geography or circumstance. He added that Mrs. Trump understands children deserve every opportunity to succeed and that their safety must always come first.

Mrs. Araneta-Marcos joined Fostering the Future Together in September, and this gathering reflects her commitment to children in the Philippines and throughout Southeast Asia. The United States applauds her leadership.

Through Fostering the Future Together, Mrs. Trump and her coalition partners are opening doors to education and technology, keeping children safe online, and preparing young people for the age of Super Intelligence (SI). First Lady Melania Trump’s message to the gathering may be viewed here.

item.title: Targeting Cyber Scam Center Enablers in Southeast Asia
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Targeting Cyber Scam Center Enablers in Southeast Asia

Press Statement

November 19, 2026

Today, the United States is sanctioning five individuals and entities that own, operate, and enable cyber scam centers in Cambodia and Burma. These criminal enterprises steal billions of dollars from victims around the world, including Americans. The Department of the Treasury designated Zhao Hui, who operated a scam center in Cambodia, and two Cambodia-based companies he controls. Treasury also designated two senior leaders of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA): commander-in-chief General Saw Shwe Wah, and Colonel Saw A One, who oversees security and participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the scam centers.

This action supports President Trump’s Executive Order 14390, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which directs the U.S. government to use every available tool against foreign-backed criminal networks that prey on Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion. Southeast Asia–based scam centers, most of them run by Chinese organized crime groups, stole an estimated $18.2 billion from Americans in 2025. These scam centers fuel human trafficking, enrich armed groups, and undermine the rule of law and stability in Southeast Asia.

The Department of the Treasury took this action in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, the Homeland Security Task Force and National Coordination Center, the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York Field Office, and the Drug Enforcement Administration.

The United States calls on governments in the region to shut down scam operations, prosecute their leaders, owners, and protectors, and identify and assist trafficking victims. The United States will keep working with partners in Southeast Asia and around the world to dismantle these networks, hold accountable those who enable them, and protect Americans from fraud.

OFAC is taking today’s actions pursuant to E.O. 13694, as amended. For more information, see Treasury’s press release.

item.title: Sanctioning Major International Drug Trafficking Organizations Linked to Foreign Terrorist Organizations
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Sanctioning Major International Drug Trafficking Organizations Linked to Foreign Terrorist Organizations

Press Statement

November 19, 2026

Today, the United States is sanctioning two international drug trafficking organizations (DTOs): the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang (Comancheros) and the Italy-based ‘Ndrangheta. Both groups provide essential logistical support to designated Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs), including the Sinaloa Cartel, Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación, and Clan del Golfo. These sanctions are being implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

The Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta play a critical role in perpetuating the global illicit drug trade. They move drug shipments, launder money, and carry out other criminal operations, enabling FTOs to extend their criminal operations across international borders and sustain global narcotics trafficking networks. These sanctions will disrupt the financial infrastructure of these DTOs, which will cut off critical support to the cartels that flood our communities with deadly drugs and help protect American lives.

The United States will pursue anyone who does business with FTOs, as well as their associated assets and criminal enterprises, wherever they try to hide. No one who finances or profits from cartel violence and destruction will find safe haven.

Today’s action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production.

For more information about today’s sanctions, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

item.title: The United States – Germany Workshop Strengthens International Cooperation Against Far-Left Terrorism
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

The United States – Germany Workshop Strengthens International Cooperation Against Far-Left Terrorism 

Press Statement

November 18, 2026

Delivering on Secretary Rubio’s announcement at the July Ministerial on the Resurgence of Political Terrorism, the U.S. Department of State and the German Federal Ministry of the Interior brought together law enforcement and counterterrorism practitioners from 31 countries for a two-day workshop this month. The workshop focused on improving information sharing and coordinating efforts to disrupt transnational far-left terrorism (FLT).

The resurgence of far-left terrorism, a form of political terrorism, increasingly overlaps with other transnational threats, including narcoterrorism as well as violent anti-Western, anti-capitalist, and antisemitic extremism. The Trump Administration is committed to shutting down safe havens and funding networks that enable far-left terrorists to operate.

item.title: U.S. Sanctions Hizballah Front Organization and Iran-Backed Financial Network
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

U.S. Sanctions Hizballah Front Organization and Iran-Backed Financial Network

Press Statement

November 18, 2026

Today, the United States is taking action against a Hizballah-affiliated front organization and smuggling network that supports the terrorist group’s activities.  The front organization, Wa Ta’awanu Association, claims to only deliver emergency relief in southern Lebanon, while, in fact, it moves Hizballah operatives, stores the group’s weapons, and channels outside donor funds toward Hizballah terrorist activities.  Its founder, Afif Abdel Rida Chouman, runs the organization at Hizballah’s direction.  By supporting Hizballah, Wa Ta’awanu undermines the sovereignty of Lebanon while jeopardizing legitimate efforts to deliver aid to the people of south Lebanon.

Today’s action also targets brothers Hassan and Ibrahim Khechen, who have, over the course of their operations, worked with Hizballah to move significant funds from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force. Their network uses Lebanon-based Gold Global Company, Türkiye-based Sankari Gold, and cash couriers to move gold bullion and currency across borders, including from Africa.

The Lebanese people deserve a sovereign, stable country in which the Lebanese state alone holds weapons and authority.  Hizballah’s continued attempts to sabotage such a future by exploiting humanitarian groups and the private sector are shameful.  The United States will continue to block such attempts while encouraging legitimate aid and investment that actually help the Lebanese people – not a Tehran-backed terrorist group.

Today’s action is being taken pursuant to the United States’ counterterrorism authority, Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended. For more information, please see Treasury’s press releases.
